input.manuscript: Liberpedia text/lp2-00.txt through text/lp2-55.txt. Runes join across page and line wraps but never across the source's nine $-delimited LP2 sections; word delimiters are hyphen, period, ampersand and section mark.
input.plain_sample: Solved GP29 rune words from the source's LP1 solved readings and LP2-56/57, excluding number-square cells; independently reconstruct the same words from Liberpedia's known-readings.json if text boundaries permit.

tests.model: For fixed plaintext rune x, c_i = c_(i-1) + (p_i-x) k_i mod29 with nonzero k_i. A cipher doublet marks exactly p_i=x.
tests.search: All 29 possible x; first a two-sided Poisson count p value for 86 events against lambda=12,947 times the solved-plaintext rate of x, then for count-compatible x an LLR of observed initial/medial/final/sole doublet locations against solved-plaintext word positions.
tests.source_gate: Exclude x if count p<1e-6 or positional LLR<=-10; report the count-compatible candidates separately. Source planted marker controls on NG, IA and EA; F two-rune-word subcheck is diagnostic, not an additional general model.
tests.limit: Depends on LP1 solved plaintext rune frequencies and word-position profile representing the unknown LP2 plaintext; fixed x and nonzero multipliers only. Does not exclude arbitrary doublet handling.

tests.model: Each used plaintext rune has one or more dedicated ciphertext runes and uses its alternatives evenly. Exactly 29 available ciphertext symbols; unused symbols are permitted.
tests.search: Enumerate every allocation of 29 ciphertext symbols across used solved-plaintext rune categories, including spare symbols left unused; minimize expected Pearson chi-square from a uniform 29-rune ciphertext of length 12,956.
tests.source_gate: Exclude this conditional family if minimum expected chi-square is at least 200. Control frequencies with an exactly flat feasible allocation must score zero; source tests the LP1 frequencies and a rare-rune smoothed sensitivity case.
tests.limit: Expected-frequency bound under even within-category choice and LP1 plaintext frequencies; not a fit of every stateful or uneven homophonic cipher, and not a direct decryption.

relationship: These are two distinct simple letter-encoding proposals, grouped for source audit and plain-language explanation. Their count/search cells are not independent discoveries of a cipher. Findings and limits must remain separate.
